sources.title: Wasmtime Security
sources.version_or_commit: Release tag v49.0.2; the inherited S10 record notes signed commit prefix 3c8a3e7; full SHA was not retrieved in this stage.
sources.locator: Security section, core WebAssembly/imports and Filesystem Access, lines 191-220.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the release-pinned official repository page and read the security overview, imports/exports boundary, and filesystem section.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WebAssembly outside-world interaction uses explicitly linked imports/exports; Wasmtime implements memory isolation; WASI filesystem access follows a capability model. The embedder chooses interfaces and filesystem access; bugs and configuration remain material.
sources.applicability: Supports a narrowly imported WASM candidate, not a claim that an embedder or this proposal is safe.

sources.title: Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: Current online Linux kernel documentation; ABI history described, no single kernel release pinned.
sources.locator: Rights associated with file descriptors and compatibility/runtime ABI detection, lines 279-308 and 368-390; kernel support, lines 877-888.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official kernel documentation; found the file-descriptor and ABI sections and read their conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Some rights are checked at open and associated with the created descriptor; pre-opened descriptors are not subject to later hierarchy restrictions. Supported rights vary by ABI; runtime detection and kernel configuration matter.
sources.applicability: Supports descriptor hygiene, runtime feature detection, and platform tests; not evidence that any proposed worker policy has been applied.

sources.title: AppContainer isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn page; inherited S15 metadata says last updated 2025-07-08; no Windows release or commit pinned.
sources.locator: Isolation and least-privilege overview, lines 31-32; inherited S15 record maps file/network/process grant discussion around lines 32-51.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official Microsoft page at its isolation overview and checked the stated purpose and least-privilege condition; the earlier S15 record preserves the full-page inspection details.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Isolation depends on resources granted to the AppContainer; the page says access beyond granted rights is restricted. Exact launch policy and resource grants remain an implementation choice.
sources.applicability: Supports considering AppContainer as a Windows candidate; does not prove a concrete launcher policy or cross-platform parity.

sources.title: VS Code Extension Runtime Security
sources.version_or_commit: Live official documentation; no immutable revision. Inherited S06 records page date 2026-10-07 and trust-prompt condition since VS Code 1.97.
sources.locator: Runtime permissions and publisher trust, lines 213-229.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and read the extension-host permissions and publisher-trust paragraphs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The extension host has VS Code's permissions, including file read/write, network requests, and external processes. Publisher trust is prompted on first third-party install under the documented release condition; it is a trust decision, not a restriction on runtime permissions.
sources.applicability: Direct evidence that process placement and publisher trust do not themselves create least-privilege runtime access.

sources.title: VS Code Extension API Reference
sources.version_or_commit: Live official API reference; no immutable revision.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the API reference at workspace.applyEdit and searched the exact all-or-nothing wording.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The documented all-or-nothing strategy applies to workspace edits consisting only of text edits. Resource creations/deletions abort subsequent edits after a failure; the method resolves to a boolean.
sources.applicability: Analogy only; the diagram editor must define and test its own transaction/rollback guarantee.
